newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close lower in choppy trading.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close lower in choppy trading.

text.p: Toronto stocks closed slightly lower on Monday, dragged down by choppy trading after triple witching last Friday, dealers said.

"The U.S. market was all over the place," said analyst Katherine Beattie with MMS International in Toronto. The volatility south of the border spread to Canada and undermined a positive start to the day, she said.

The Toronto Stock Exchange 300 Composite Index closed down 6.76 points at 5,862.90 with 72.22 million shares worth US$627.62 million (C$857.87 million) trading hands. Decliners outnumbered advancers 514 to 479 with 303 unchanged.
On Friday, trading was dominated by the triple witching expiry of options, index options and futures.

Six of the TSE's sub-groups closed higher on Monday, while eight closed lower. Real estate led the way, gaining 20.18 points or 0.89 percent to close at 2278.15. On the down side, transportation lost the most, down 0.96 percent or 59.95 points to 6210.54.
Metals and minerals also lost ground, falling 0.77 percent after Lehman Brothers cut its rating for Inco Ltd. to neutral from outperform. Inco fell C$1.25 to C$43.65.
"The fact that we didn't go higher today is a very big problem," said Beattie. Usually the TSE 300 rises as Christmas approaches, she said.

"What we're seeing is any time the market is up, we get more sellers in the market closing their portfolios, locking in their profits and sitting on the sidelines," she added. "The market is still really fragile."

The possibility of a deal between Bre-X Minerals Ltd. and Barrick Gold Corp. kept traders' attention again on Monday. Bre-X said it was still awaiting approval from the Indonesian government before announcing the terms of the deal.
